2	import { PickFolder, ScanLocalRoot } from '../../../../wailsjs/go/main/App'
3	import { LocalFile, LocalFileGroup } from '../types'
4	
5	// Flat, ordered list of every file in the tree (a group's own files, then
6	// its subgroups' files, recursively). Shared by the upload worker (order to
7	// process files in), the upload modal's per-group rollup counts, and the
8	// "every file in this group is done" check driving the Open-in-Drive link —
9	// one traversal so they can't drift out of sync on how they handle nesting.
10	export function flattenFiles(group: LocalFileGroup): LocalFile[] {
11	  return [...group.files, ...group.subgroups.flatMap(flattenFiles)]
12	}
13	
14	export interface FileTreeHandle {
15	  root: string | null
16	  tree: LocalFileGroup | null
17	  loading: boolean
18	  error: string | null
19	  // Resolves to whether a folder was actually picked (false if the user
20	  // cancelled the dialog), so callers know when a fresh root replaced the
21	  // previous one and any per-root state (e.g. the upload queue) should reset.
22	  pickRoot: () => Promise<boolean>
23	}
24	
25	// Owns the currently scanned local folder: which root the user picked, the
26	// resulting file/subgroup tree, and loading/error state while ScanLocalRoot
27	// runs. The scan is an async Go RPC that can fail (bad permissions, folder
28	// moved/deleted mid-pick, etc.), so this state needs to live outside the
29	// tree itself — callers can show a spinner or an error message instead of
30	// rendering a stale or partial tree while a scan is in flight.
31	export function useFileTree(): FileTreeHandle {
32	  const [root, setRoot] = useState<string | null>(null)
33	  const [tree, setTree] = useState<LocalFileGroup | null>(null)
34	  const [loading, setLoading] = useState(false)
35	  const [error, setError] = useState<string | null>(null)
36	
37	  const pickRoot = useCallback(async () => {
38	    const folder = await PickFolder('Choose Root Folder')
39	    if (!folder) return false
40	
41	    setRoot(folder)
42	    setLoading(true)
43	    setError(null)
44	    try {
45	      setTree(await ScanLocalRoot(folder))
46	    } catch (e) {
47	      setTree(null)
48	      setError(String(e))
49	    } finally {
50	      setLoading(false)
51	    }
52	    return true
53	  }, [])
54	
55	  return { root, tree, loading, error, pickRoot }
56	}

1	import { useState, useCallback, useEffect } from 'react'
2	import { flattenFiles } from './useFileTree'
3	import { LocalFileGroup } from '../types'
4	
5	export type GroupSelectionState = 'checked' | 'unchecked' | 'indeterminate'
6	
7	export interface InclusionHandle {
8	  isFileSelected: (path: string) => boolean
9	  getGroupState: (group: LocalFileGroup) => GroupSelectionState
10	  toggleFile: (path: string) => void
11	  toggleGroup: (group: LocalFileGroup) => void
12	  selectAll: () => void
13	  selectNone: () => void
14	}
15	
16	// Tracks which files are excluded from the upload, keyed by path. A
17	// subfolder's checkbox state is derived from its descendant files rather
18	// than stored separately, so the "fully selected/unselected collapses all
19	// the way up the tree" behavior falls out of the derivation for free
20	// instead of needing explicit upward-propagation bookkeeping.
21	export function useInclusion(tree: LocalFileGroup | null): InclusionHandle {
22	  const [deselected, setDeselected] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set())
23	
24	  // Resets to fully-selected on every fresh scan — deliberately not
25	  // persisted, unlike Drive folder mappings.
26	  useEffect(() => {
27	    setDeselected(new Set())
28	  }, [tree])
29	
30	  const isFileSelected = useCallback((path: string) => !deselected.has(path), [deselected])
31	
32	  const getGroupState = useCallback((group: LocalFileGroup): GroupSelectionState => {
33	    const files = flattenFiles(group)
34	    if (files.length === 0) return 'checked'
35	    const selectedCount = files.filter(f => !deselected.has(f.path)).length
36	    if (selectedCount === 0) return 'unchecked'
37	    if (selectedCount === files.length) return 'checked'
38	    return 'indeterminate'
39	  }, [deselected])
40	
41	  const toggleFile = useCallback((path: string) => {
42	    setDeselected(prev => {
43	      const next = new Set(prev)
44	      if (next.has(path)) next.delete(path); else next.add(path)
45	      return next
46	    })
47	  }, [])
48	
49	  // Indeterminate or fully-unselected groups select all descendants; a
50	  // fully-selected group deselects all descendants. Decided from the
51	  // group's own current state rather than the checkbox's native toggle, so
52	  // clicking an indeterminate checkbox always selects, never clears.
53	  const toggleGroup = useCallback((group: LocalFileGroup) => {
54	    const files = flattenFiles(group)
55	    setDeselected(prev => {
56	      const allSelected = files.every(f => !prev.has(f.path))
57	      const next = new Set(prev)
58	      for (const f of files) {
59	        if (allSelected) next.add(f.path); else next.delete(f.path)
60	      }
61	      return next
62	    })
63	  }, [])
64	
65	  const selectAll = useCallback(() => setDeselected(new Set()), [])
66	
67	  const selectNone = useCallback(() => {
68	    setDeselected(new Set(tree ? flattenFiles(tree).map(f => f.path) : []))
69	  }, [tree])
70	
71	  return { isFileSelected, getGroupState, toggleFile, toggleGroup, selectAll, selectNone }

12	  // Plain click: replaces the selection with just this item.

19	// highlighting and (Step 3e) batch Drive folder assignment — a single
20	// selection concept rather than a separate preview-only highlight.
21	export function useSelection(tree: LocalFileGroup | null): SelectionHandle {
22	  const [selected, setSelected] = useState<Map<string, SelectionItem>>(new Map())
23	
24	  // Resets on every fresh scan, like inclusion — a new root's rows aren't
25	  // the ones that were selected under the old one.
26	  useEffect(() => {
27	    setSelected(new Map())
28	  }, [tree])
29	
30	  const isSelected = useCallback((item: SelectionItem) => selected.has(itemKey(item)), [selected])
31

33	    setSelected(new Map([[itemKey(item), item]]))

37	    setSelected(prev => {

35	    setFileOverrides(prev => new Map(prev).set(filePath, assignment))
36	  }, [])

49	// Effective Drive assignment for every file in the tree: its own override,
50	// else the nearest ancestor group's assignment, else null. Mirrors the
51	// inheritance walk GroupNode/FileList do inline during render (same
52	// groupKey scheme: joined by '/', rooted at each top-level subgroup's own
53	// name), but usable outside a render tree — e.g. to check whether every
54	// file is ready to upload, or to build an upload job list.
55	export function resolveEffectiveAssignments(
56	  tree: LocalFileGroup,
57	  { groupAssignments, fileOverrides }: Pick<DriveAssignmentsHandle, 'groupAssignments' | 'fileOverrides'>
58	): Map<string, DriveAssignment | null> {
59	  const result = new Map<string, DriveAssignment | null>()
60	
61	  const walk = (group: LocalFileGroup, groupKey: string | null, inherited: DriveAssignment | null) => {
62	    const effective = (groupKey !== null ? groupAssignments.get(groupKey) : undefined) ?? inherited
63	    for (const file of group.files) {
64	      result.set(file.path, fileOverrides.get(file.path) ?? effective)
65	    }
66	    for (const sub of group.subgroups) {
67	      walk(sub, groupKey !== null ? `${groupKey}/${sub.name}` : sub.name, effective)
68	    }
69	  }

23	// LocalFileGroup is one folder's worth of files, plus its nested
24	// subfolders. Name is "" only for the root LocalFileGroup returned by
25	// ScanLocalRoot; every subgroup has a real folder name.
26	type LocalFileGroup struct {
27		Name      string           `json:"name"`
28		Files     []LocalFile      `json:"files"`
29		Subgroups []LocalFileGroup `json:"subgroups"`
30	}
31	
32	// ScanLocalRoot scans root recursively and returns it as a LocalFileGroup:
33	// its own direct files in Files, and every subdirectory (at any depth) as a
34	// nested Subgroups entry. Unlike a subfolder, the root is always returned
35	// even if it's entirely empty, so the UI has something to render a "no
36	// files" state from.
37	func ScanLocalRoot(root string) (LocalFileGroup, error) {
38		return scanDirectory(root, "")
39	}
40	
41	// scanDirectory scans dir's direct entries in a single pass: each file
42	// becomes a LocalFile, each non-hidden subdirectory is scanned recursively
43	// (skipping symlinks) and — if its subtree contains no files at all — is
44	// omitted from Subgroups. name is used as the returned group's Name (pass ""
45	// for the scan root). PDFs whose page count can't be read are still
46	// included, flagged via LocalFile.Corrupt, rather than dropped from the
47	// scan; non-PDF files are never considered corrupt.
48	//
49	// Both slice fields are always initialized to non-nil (even when empty),
50	// since a nil Go slice marshals to JSON `null` rather than `[]`, which
51	// crashes the frontend (e.g. `group.subgroups.length` throws on null).
52	func scanDirectory(dir, name string) (LocalFileGroup, error) {
53		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
54		if err != nil {
55			return LocalFileGroup{}, err
56		}
57	
58		files := []LocalFile{}
59		subgroups := []LocalFileGroup{}
60	
61		for _, e := range entries {
62			entryName := e.Name()
63			if strings.HasPrefix(entryName, ".") {
64				continue
65			}
66	
67			if e.IsDir() {
68				// os.DirEntry.IsDir() reflects the directory entry itself rather
69				// than a resolved symlink target, so a symlinked directory
70				// (including one that would otherwise form a loop) never enters
71				// this branch — it's simply skipped.
72				sub, err := scanDirectory(filepath.Join(dir, entryName), entryName)
73				if err != nil {
74					return LocalFileGroup{}, err
75				}
76				if len(sub.Files) > 0 || len(sub.Subgroups) > 0 {
77					subgroups = append(subgroups, sub)
78				}
79				continue
80			}
81	
82			path := filepath.Join(dir, entryName)
83			info, err := os.Stat(path)
84			if err != nil {
85				continue
86			}
87	
88			isPDF := strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(entryName), ".pdf")
89			var count int
90			var corrupt bool
91			if isPDF {
92				count, err = pdf.PageCount(path)
93				corrupt = err != nil
94			}
95			files = append(files, LocalFile{
96				Path:      path,
97				Name:      entryName,
98				SizeBytes: info.Size(),
99				IsPDF:     isPDF,
100				PageCount: count,
101				Corrupt:   corrupt,
102			})
103		}

105		return LocalFileGroup{Name: name, Files: files, Subgroups: subgroups}, nil

message.content: What's your reasoning to name the prop `key`? Isn't it rather a `path`, like in LocalFile?

content.text:
Two reasons, one about the existing codebase and one about what the value actually is:

1. **The feature's vocabulary is already "key," not "path."** `SelectionItem` already has `{ type: 'group', key: string }`, `useDriveAssignments`'s `groupAssignments` map is keyed by a `groupKey` parameter, and `pruneSelection.ts` has `selectedGroupKeys`/`parentGroupKey`/`fileParentKeys`. If `LocalFileGroup.key` were named `path`, the field would read differently from every variable that consumes it — you'd have `group.path` flowing into a parameter called `groupKey` and landing in `SelectionItem.key`.

2. **It isn't the same kind of value as `LocalFile.path`.** `LocalFile.path` is an absolute, OS-native filesystem path built by Go's `filepath.Join` (backslash-separated on Windows). The group identifier is always forward-slash-joined folder *names*, relative to the picked scan root, built in JS — on a Windows machine it never matches a real filesystem path at all. Calling both `path` would suggest they're comparable/interchangeable when they're actually different coordinate systems.

If you'd still rather have `path`, I'd lean toward renaming the other "key" spots to match rather than mixing the two — happy to do either, just say which.

content.text:
Wails v2.12.0. This confirms the mechanism.

**How Wails names it:** When you run `wails dev`/`wails build` (which invokes the bindings generator internally), Wails statically parses the Go source of your bound struct — here, `*App`, registered via `wails.Run(&options.App{Bind: []interface{}{app}})` in `app.go`/`main.go`. For each exported method (`ScanLocalRoot`), it resolves the full signature using Go's type-checker over the package graph, not just reflection — so it sees the return type is a named struct `LocalFileGroup` declared in `package filetree` (`backend/filetree/filetree.go`).

It then:
- Emits that struct once into `frontend/wailsjs/go/models.ts`, wrapped in `export namespace filetree { export class LocalFileGroup {...} }` — the namespace name comes from the Go package's own `package filetree` declaration, not the import path or any alias.
- In `App.d.ts`, references it as `filetree.LocalFileGroup` (importing `{filetree}` from `../models`), qualifying with the package namespace specifically so two different packages that both happen to declare a `Foo` struct don't collide.

So `filetree.LocalFileGroup` isn't a name Wails invents — it's mechanically derived from `backend/filetree`'s package name plus the struct's own name, which is why our own hand-written `types.ts` `LocalFileGroup` (no namespace, plus the extra `key` field) is a distinct, structurally-compatible type rather than the same one Wails generated.

An earlier "commit" instruction does not authorize committing again later in the session — each commit (or batch of commits for one piece of work) needs its own explicit go-ahead. This is about the approval relationship with this specific user — a different user of this repo might not want that friction at all — so it belongs in memory, not CLAUDE.md. See [[feedback_memory_vs_claudemd]].

**How to apply:** Finish the work, run verification (build/test/typecheck), summarize what changed, and explicitly ask "want me to commit this?" — then wait. Do not commit proactively even if the previous turn's work was committed after a similar request. This applies within a single session and especially across multiple pieces of work in a row (e.g. a multi-step checklist implementation) — each step's commit needs its own confirmation, not just the first one. See also [[feedback_separate_commits]] for how to split what does get committed once confirmed.

Writing the message to a file sidesteps shell quoting entirely — apostrophes, quotes, backticks are all safe in file content. `-F` also naturally satisfies the "show the message first" rule above, since the file is written (and can be shown) before the commit runs. This is purely a workaround for how *I* invoke shell commands in this sandboxed environment — not relevant to a human contributor or a rule about repo content — so it's memory, not CLAUDE.md.

**Skip `git status` / `git add`, pass pathspecs straight to `git commit` (added 2026-07-10):** Default commit command is now `git commit -F <message-file> -- <path1> <path2> ...`, listing exactly the files touched this turn. `git commit <pathspec>` stages and commits only those paths' current working-tree content, regardless of what else is dirty elsewhere — no preceding `git add` needed. `git status` is skippable too since I already know which files I edited from my own tool calls this session; I don't need to discover that via status. Why: user asked for a leaner commit flow after watching the status→add→commit dance every time. Caveat: this repo has had stray unrelated modified files show up before (e.g. `frontend/wailsjs/runtime/*` regenerated by a `wails dev` run outside the session) — always naming explicit paths on `git commit` is what keeps those out, so don't switch to `git commit -a` or `git add -A` even though they'd also skip the status/add dance.
